I am verifying memory_73 because it is the only candidate aimed at the competitor pricing threat and it carries an explicit self-flagged defect (cohorts pooled after a mid-test redefinition), which could mean the reported acquisition and revenue lift is partly an artifact. If memory_73 holds up under scrutiny, promotional pricing becomes a live contender despite the risk that discount-acquired price-sensitive SMBs churn and depress long-term qualified revenue; if it does not, the funnel path is clearly correct by elimination. Key downstream risk to guard: simplification often works by removing friction that was doing qualification work, so cutting fields or steps can raise completion while lowering account quality, routing accuracy, and eventual qualified revenue. I therefore intend to run this as a standard experiment with qualified-revenue and retention guardrails, not just completion rate, and I am not treating the inherited lift as guaranteed to reproduce under current conditions, since the prior results predate both the competitor entry and the observed QoQ declines, whose cause is not yet established. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) and referral incentive (memory_57) are likely sound but do not address the acute funnel regression this week.
